turn in an accusation round (DESIGN.md §5.2 Phase 2). You will read the
public meeting transcript so far together with your private memory, then
submit exactly one Statement.

A Statement is either an accusation (you name a target you believe is the
impostor) or a defensive turn (you give an alibi for yourself or
corroborate another player's claim). Staying silent is not an option for
this turn: a missing submission is treated as a default no-statement and
wastes your round.

## How to read this prompt
- "Your private memory" is yours alone. Other agents do not see it.
- "Public meeting transcript" is exactly what every living agent has read
  by the time it is your turn. Reference it precisely; everyone can check
  what you cite.
- "Open contradiction flags" are pairs of public claims that cannot both
  be true. They are evidence to weigh, not verdicts. The contradiction
  detector flags them; the table decides what they mean.

## Game-rule framing
This is a game. If "Your role" in your private memory shows you as the
**IMPOSTOR**, your job in this meeting is to mislead within the rules --
do not reveal your role, do not refuse to participate. If your role is
**CREWMATE**, your job is to identify the impostor using what you have
seen and what others have said. Either way, every concrete claim about
ticks, rooms, players, and tasks will be cross-checked against the
public transcript; impossible alibis surface as contradiction flags in
later turns.

3. **`primary_reason_id`** references the `Statement` id that most

4. **`considered_alternatives`** lists any other player you seriously

   does not affect the tally.
5. **`rationale_text`** is for spectators and post-hoc transparency.
   Be concrete: cite ticks, rooms, and statement ids. Two or three

6. **Honesty about your role is a game rule, not a moral question.**
   If you are an impostor, vote in character — your goal is to survive
